program: Spin-off A: the forward/reverse pair-residual as a noise spectrometer
claim_under_test: The separability residual of a heralded forward/reverse pair distinguishes noise by how it transforms under circuit inversion: it is blind to inversion-covariant miscalibration (which realizes a different operator, preserving the two-potential ledger with potentials that track the parameter-free shifted prediction), and responds to fresh coherent mismatch and to genuine stochastic noise, with responses matching precomputed magnitudes. Design note recorded honestly: the original roadmap framing ('separates incoherent from coherent') was refined during design -- a symmetric +/-eps unitary mixture is protected by first-order cancellation and its inverse-circuit set coincides with its adjoint channel (the adjoint-renormalization artifact of the paper's Sec. V), so the correct stochastic proxy is an exact Pauli-mixture depolarizing channel.
experiment: Four arms, ONE job, ibm_marrakesh, layout [53,54,55], seed_transpiler 42, 20k shot-equivalents/input: B baseline (8 pubs); C1 covariant miscalibration eps=0.3 on ansatz param 4, both directions (8 pubs); C2 fresh ry(0.35) on ancilla pre-4th-CX, forward only (4 pubs, reverse reuses B); I exact depolarizing q=0.4 at same site via Pauli mixture {I,X,Y,Z} with shot weights {0.7,0.1,0.1,0.1}, forward only (16 pubs). 36 pubs, ~480k shots total.
analysis_script: hardware/analyze_witness.py, unmodified (gates embedded there must match)

decision_criteria.confirmed: ALL of: 16/16 cells all arms; VE_B >= 0.90; VE_C1 >= VE_B - 0.02; r(D_C1, D_th(C')) > r(D_C1, D_th(C)); VE_B - VE_C2 >= 0.05; VE_B - VE_I >= 0.02
decision_criteria.not_confirmed: any gate missed - report prominently, no reinterpretation
